title: Set 282

sentences.ko: 아 진짜, 5분만 앉아 있으면 누가 꼭 만나는 사람 있냐고 물어보는 거야. 이모는 모두 있는 앞에서 왜 아직도 월세 사냐고 묻기까지 했어. 그래서 일어날 핑계 만들려고 계속 사람들한테 마실 거 갖다줄까 하고 물어봤어.
sentences.text: Oh my god, I couldn't sit down for five minutes without somebody asking if I'm seeing anyone. My aunt even asked why I'm still renting, in front of everybody, so I just kept offering to get people drinks so I'd have an excuse to get up.

alts.text: Seriously, every five minutes somebody's asking if I'm seeing anyone. My aunt even asked why I'm still renting, right in front of everyone, so I just kept offering to grab people drinks so I'd have an excuse to get up.

Honestly, I could not sit down for five minutes without someone asking whether I was seeing anyone. My aunt even asked, in front of everyone, why I was still renting, so I kept offering to get people drinks in order to have a reason to stand up.

sentences.note: **seeing anyone** 은 사귀는 사람이 있다는 뜻이에요. **have an excuse to** 는 ~할 핑계가 있다는 말로, 자리를 뜨고 싶을 때 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 주말 내내 아무것도 안 했는데 후회 하나도 안 해. 빨래라도 해야지 하고 계속 생각만 하다가 그냥 소파에 붙어 있었는데, 솔직히 오늘이 한 달 만에 제일 개운해.
sentences.text: I didn't do a single thing all weekend, and I'm not even sorry. I kept telling myself I should at least do laundry, but I just stayed on the couch, and honestly, I feel better today than I have in like a month.

alts.text: Did absolutely nothing all weekend and I'm not even sorry. Kept telling myself I should at least do laundry, but I just stayed on the couch, and honestly I feel better today than I have in like a month.

I did not do a single thing all weekend, and I do not regret it. I kept telling myself that I should at least do the laundry, but I remained on the couch, and I feel better today than I have in about a month.

sentences.note: **not even sorry** 는 전혀 후회 안 한다는 뜻으로, 당당하게 말할 때 써요. **than I have in like a month** 는 한 달 만에 제일 그렇다는 말이에요. like 는 대충 그쯤이라는 느낌이에요.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 캠핑 가기로 했는데, 토요일 밤에 천둥번개가 친다고 해서 그냥 당일치기 등산만 하기로 했어. 비만 오는 거면 그래도 갔을 텐데, 번개 치는데 텐트에서 자는 건 싫어.
sentences.text: We were supposed to go camping this weekend, but they're saying there's a thunderstorm coming Saturday night, so we're just doing a day hike instead. I mean, if it was only rain I'd still go, but I'm not sleeping in a tent with lightning around.

alts.text: So camping was the plan this weekend, but there's supposed to be a thunderstorm Saturday night, so we're just doing a day hike. If it was just rain I'd still go, but I'm not sleeping in a tent with lightning around.

We had planned to go camping this weekend, but a thunderstorm is forecast for Saturday night, so we will take a day hike instead. If it were only rain, I would still go, but I am not willing to sleep in a tent with lightning nearby.

sentences.note: **they're saying** 은 일기예보나 사람들 말로는 ~래, 할 때 써요. **day hike** 는 하루에 다녀오는 등산이에요.

sentences.ko: 늦어서 미안해, 밤에 충전기 꽂는 걸 깜빡해서 폰이 꺼져 있었고, 그래서 알람이 아예 안 울렸어. 문자라도 했을 텐데, 집에서 뛰어나갈 때까지 몇 시인지도 몰랐어.
sentences.text: Sorry I'm late, my phone died overnight because I forgot to plug it in, so my alarm never went off. I would've texted you, but I didn't even realize what time it was until I was running out the door.

alts.text: My bad, my phone died overnight since I forgot to charge it, so my alarm never went off. I would've texted, but I had no clue what time it was till I was running out the door.

I apologize for being late. My phone ran out of battery overnight because I forgot to charge it, so my alarm did not go off. I would have sent you a message, but I did not realize what time it was until I was already leaving.

sentences.note: **my phone died** 는 폰 배터리가 다 됐다는 뜻이에요. **went off** 는 알람이 울린다는 말로, never went off 하면 안 울렸다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 응, 다 괜찮아요, 아빠. 일이 좀 정신없긴 한데 좋은 쪽으로 정신없는 거라 걱정 안 하셔도 돼요. 그건 그렇고 제 얘기는 이제 됐고, 무릎은 병원 가서 보셨어요?
sentences.text: Yeah, everything's fine, Dad. Work's been kind of crazy, but it's the good kind of crazy, so don't worry about it. Anyway, enough about me, did you ever get your knee looked at?

alts.text: Dad, I'm fine, really. Work's kinda nuts, but it's the good kind of nuts, so don't worry. Anyway, enough about me, did you ever get your knee checked out?
Yes, everything is fine, Dad. Work has been rather hectic, but in a good way, so please do not worry about it. In any case, enough about me. Did you ever have your knee examined?

sentences.note: **the good kind of crazy** 는 바쁘지만 즐거운 정신없음을 말해요. **enough about me** 는 내 얘기는 그만하고 화제를 상대에게 돌릴 때 써요. **get your knee looked at** 은 무릎을 진찰받다는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

reviewed: 1번 formal: 같은 문장 안에서 was 와 am 이 섞여 있어 시제를 맞춤 (why I was still renting)
2번 note: I feel better than I have in a month 는 문장에 이 모양 그대로 나오지 않음. 문장에 실제로 있는 than I have in like a month 로 바꿈
2번 한국어: 미안하지도 않아 는 번역투라 후회 하나도 안 해 로 바꿈
4번 한국어: 문자라도 보냈어야 했는데 는 I should have 의 뜻임. 영어 I would've texted you 에 맞춰 문자라도 했을 텐데 로 바꿈
